questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

The price of petrol **has increased yesterday.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**has increased yesterday**" is incorrect because the present perfect tense ("has increased") cannot be used with a specific time reference like "yesterday."
 
• Instead, the simple past tense ("**rose yesterday**" or "**increased yesterday**") is appropriate when referring to a specific event that occurred in the past.
 
• Option 2, "**increased yesterday**," is the most grammatically correct and concise choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The price of petrol increased yesterday."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "rose yesterday" is grammatically correct but may not be the best choice depending on the context. "Rose" is less commonly used in this particular sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** "has been increased yesterday" is incorrect because the present perfect tense ("has been increased") cannot be paired with "yesterday," which is a specific past time.
 
• **Option 4:** "risen yesterday" is incorrect because "risen" requires an auxiliary verb to form a proper sentence (e.g., "has risen yesterday").

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct to Indirect Speech.

They said, "How foolish of him to say that!"

options.text: They exclaimed how foolish of him to say that.
They exclaimed that it had been very foolish of him to say that.
They exclaimed that he is very foolish to say that.
They said it was very foolish of him to say that.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** They exclaimed how foolish of him to say that.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Exclamation:**
 
 
• Direct speech exclamation "How foolish of him to say that!" is converted to "They exclaimed how foolish of him to say that."
 
• The tone of surprise and criticism is maintained.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• Direct speech reporting verb "said" is converted to "exclaimed" to match the exclamatory tone.
 
 
 
• **Tense:**
 
 
• Since the sentence is universal in nature, tense remains unchanged.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech exclamation is removed.
 
• Sentence is restructured to fit indirect speech format.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They exclaimed how foolish of him to say that."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "They exclaimed that it had been very foolish of him to say that." 

 
 
• Incorrect tense conversion changes the meaning unnecessarily.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "They exclaimed that he is very foolish to say that."
 
 
• Incorrect tense (present tense "is" instead of past tense).
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "They said it was very foolish of him to say that."
 
 
• Fails to convey the exclamatory tone.

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

Human memory is a complex neurological process.

P: Short-term memory stores data temporarily for immediate use.

Q: Information can be transferred to long-term memory with repetition.

R: The brain filters and encodes information efficiently.

S: Long-term memory holds information for an extended period.

6. Understanding memory helps improve learning strategies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph begins by introducing human memory as a complex neurological process and proceeds to explain its components logically.
 
• **Sentence R is the first sentence** because it introduces the brain's role in filtering and encoding information efficiently:
 
 
• "The brain filters and encodes information efficiently."
 
 
 
• **Sentence P follows** as it explains the function of short-term memory:
 
 
• "Short-term memory stores data temporarily for immediate use."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the third sentence** because it elaborates on long-term memory:
 
 
• "Long-term memory holds information for an extended period."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q is the fourth** as it explains how information is transferred to long-term memory through repetition:
 
 
• "Information can be transferred to long-term memory with repetition."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **RPSQ**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Human memory is a complex neurological process. The brain filters and encodes information efficiently. Short-term memory stores data temporarily for immediate use. questions.question: Select the synonym of **Vicinity.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Proximity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

 
• The word **"Vicinity"** refers to the area near or surrounding a particular place; it is synonymous with closeness or nearness. (नजदीकी, आस-पास)

 

 
• **Example:** There were several restaurants in the vicinity of the hotel.

 

 

 
• **"Proximity"** means closeness or nearness in space, time, or relationship; it is used to indicate being close to something. (निकटता)

 

 
• **Example:** The proximity of the school to her house made it convenient for the children to attend classes.

 

 

 
• Hence, we can infer that the synonym of **'Vicinity'** is **'Proximity'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Proximity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** His absence from the meeting was noticeable.

 

 

 
• **Distance** (दूरी): The amount of space between two things or people.

 

 
• **Example:** The distance between the two towns is approximately 50 kilometers.

 

 

 
• **Departure** (प्रस्थान): The act of leaving a place.

 

 
• **Example:** The departure of the train was delayed due to weather conditions.
